optimized_o2_instruction_counts.interpretation: In the optimized diagnostic binary, about 95.5% of RossFast solve instructions are inside the repeated candidate-step path.

noinline_structural_crosscheck.interpretation_boundary: This no-inline build is a structural instruction decomposition, not a production CPU-time percentage. Its dynamic call counts exactly reproduce the known algorithmic topology, so it is valid for locating work, not for claiming wall-time shares.

one_time_initialization_observation.claim_boundary: RossFast table/provider initialization was intentionally outside the F-ROSS15 timed solver region. This large one-time cost must not be folded into the solver-seam slowdown ratio; its application-level importance depends on reuse/amortization.

scientific_interpretation: The current RossFast slowdown is not caused primarily by the small 16x16 tridiagonal linear solve. RossFast pays for 24 candidate steps per solver call to construct its coarse-plus-two-half temporal certificate. In the optimized binary those candidate steps account for about 95.5% of solve-path instructions. The structural no-inline decomposition places about 31.9% of candidate-step instructions in inverse-capacity evaluation, 29.8% in table-face linearization, 21.8% in water-content-to-head inversion, and only 5.8% in the tridiagonal factor-and-solve. The first three transformation categories together account for about 83.6% of candidate-step instructions in that structural diagnostic.
next_permitted_action: Use these diagnostics to design a separate optimization study. The highest-value questions are whether the temporal certificate can avoid recomputing three full 8-step trajectories and whether repeated capacity/head/table transforms can be cached or algebraically reduced without changing qualified semantics. No such optimization is admitted by F-ROSS16D1.
